mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.4 percentage points for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% and a decline in UNRATE below 3.5% signals a labor market expansion with stable unemployment, which boosts consumer spending and supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below -0.3% for two months signals weakening consumer and housing demand, which reduces economic activity and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month - 0.3% AND HOUST < previous month - 0.3% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly FEDFUNDS rate below 1% for six consecutive months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which supports risk asset valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.6% and RSAFS above 2% signals a supply-side expansion with rising corporate investment, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during a non-recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.6% AND RSAFS > previous month + 2% AND UNRATE > 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered non-recessionary episodes.
